test_title: SSC Stenographer 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 11 Dec, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following Acts had provided the establishment of the Federal Court in British India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**The Government of India Act, 1935**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Government of India Act, 1935, led to the establishment of a Federal Court in British India.
 
• The Federal Court was inaugurated on 1 October 1937 and was located in Delhi.
 
• The court had original, appellate, and advisory jurisdiction to resolve disputes between the provinces and the central government.
 
• Sir Maurice Gwyer served as the first Chief Justice of the Federal Court.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Government of India Act, 1935**

 
 
• The Act was the longest act passed by the British Parliament at the time.
 
• It provided for the establishment of an All-India Federation and provincial autonomy.
 
• It was divided into 14 parts and had 321 sections and 10 schedules.
 
• It laid down the foundation for a federal structure in India, which was later adopted in the Constitution of India.
 
 
 
• **Federal Court of India**
 
 
• The Federal Court acted as the precursor to the Supreme Court of India, which was established on 28 January 1950.
 
• Its decisions could be appealed to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in London.
 
• The court's jurisdiction covered civil, criminal, and constitutional matters.
 
• It was an important institution for the judicial administration in pre-independence India.
 
 
 
• **Sir Maurice Gwyer**
 
 
• He served as the Chief Justice of the Federal Court from 1937 to 1943.
 
• He played a significant role in laying down the judicial principles that were later followed by the Supreme Court of India.
 
• His judgments were instrumental in interpreting the provisions of the Government of India Act, 1935.
